group.passage:
In 1990, about 43 percent of the world's people lived in extreme poverty, which the World Bank now defines as living on less than $3.00 a day. The Bank raised the line from $2.15 in June 2025, and it uses prices adjusted for what money can buy in each country, so the line stands for roughly the same basket of basic goods everywhere rather than the same sum of local money. By 2020 the global share had fallen to about 11 percent, but behind this single average lie very different regional stories, as the chart below shows.
The most dramatic change took place in East Asia and the Pacific, which in 1990 had the highest rate of the four groups shown, about two people in every three. Rapid economic growth, above all in China, then cut the rate in every period on the chart, and by 2020 it was below 3 percent. China's own rate dropped from 83.1 percent in 1990 to almost nothing by 2019.
South Asia started lower but moved more slowly at first: its rate barely changed for more than ten years and still stood at about 46 percent in 2002. After that, however, the decline sped up sharply, and by 2020 the region's rate had fallen below the world average.
Sub-Saharan Africa followed a different path. Its rate rose during the early 1990s and was still above 60 percent in 2002. Although it has fallen since then, the fall has been slow, and the rate edged up again by 2020. Meanwhile, the region's population more than doubled, so a lower rate did not mean fewer poor people. About 320 million people in the region lived in extreme poverty in 1990, but by 2020 the number had grown to roughly 537 million.
The result is a very different map of need. According to the World Bank, the number of people living in extreme poverty worldwide fell from around 2.3 billion in 1990 to around 831 million in 2025, mainly thanks to growth in East and South Asia. Those who remain are increasingly found in Sub-Saharan Africa and in places troubled by conflict, and nearly three in four of them live in the countryside. The World Bank hopes to bring the global rate below 3 percent by 2030, yet its own forecasts suggest that about 9 percent of the world's people will still be extremely poor that year.

1.strategy_zh: 折線圖上同時有好幾個交叉點時，先確認題目問的是「哪兩條線」，再逐年比較這兩條線的數值，找出大小關係改變的那一段。

translation_zh.text:
1990 年，全世界約 43% 的人生活在赤貧之中；世界銀行現在把赤貧定義為每天生活費不到 3.00 美元。世界銀行在 2025 年 6 月把這條線從 2.15 美元調高，而且它使用依各國購買力調整過的價格，所以這條線在各地代表的是大致相同的一籃基本物品，而不是相同金額的當地貨幣。到了 2020 年，全球的比例已降到約 11%；然而在這個單一的平均數背後，各地區的故事截然不同，如下圖所示。
變化最劇烈的是東亞與太平洋地區。1990 年，它是圖中四組裡比例最高的，大約每三個人就有兩個赤貧。快速的經濟成長（尤其是在中國）讓這個比例在圖上的每一段時間都下降，到 2020 年已低於 3%。中國本身的比例則從 1990 年的 83.1% 降到 2019 年的幾乎為零。
南亞的起點較低，但一開始進展較慢：十多年間比例幾乎沒有變化，2002 年仍約為 46%。不過在那之後，下降速度大幅加快，到 2020 年，該地區的比例已低於世界平均。
撒哈拉以南非洲走的是另一條路。它的比例在 1990 年代初期上升，2002 年仍高於 60%。雖然之後一直在下降，但降得很慢，到 2020 年又小幅回升。同時，該地區的人口增加了一倍以上，所以比例降低並不代表窮人變少。1990 年，該地區約有 3.2 億人生活在赤貧中；到了 2020 年，人數增加到約 5.37 億。
結果是一張非常不同的「需求地圖」。根據世界銀行，全世界的赤貧人數從 1990 年的約 23 億，降到 2025 年的約 8.31 億，主要歸功於東亞和南亞的經濟成長。剩下的赤貧人口越來越集中在撒哈拉以南非洲和受衝突困擾的地方，而且其中將近四分之三住在鄉村。世界銀行希望在 2030 年前把全球比例降到 3% 以下，但它自己的預測顯示，那一年仍會有約 9% 的世界人口處於赤貧。
【圖】折線圖：每日生活費低於 3.00 美元（2021 PPP）的人口比例（%），1990、1996、2002、2008、2014、2020 年。世界 43.4、38.1、33.7、24.1、14.5、11.4；東亞與太平洋 67、52、40、23.4、7.8、2.7；南亞 49.7、46.8、46、36.8、20、9.4；撒哈拉以南非洲 61.5、63.9、60.8、51.9、45.3、46。

open_tasks.prompt: A classmate says, “Extreme poverty is almost solved, because the global rate fell from about 43 percent to about 11 percent.” Based on the passage and the chart, write 1–2 English sentences explaining what this view leaves out.
reference_answers: The global rate hides big differences between regions; in Sub-Saharan Africa the rate is still around 46 percent, and the number of extremely poor people there has actually grown.
It leaves out that hundreds of millions of people are still extremely poor and that they are more and more concentrated in Sub-Saharan Africa and places affected by conflict.
